notes:
Batch C (atorvastatin, simvastatin, clopidogrel, warfarin, phytomenadione). All quotes checked FOUND with fetchtext --check on 2026-10-17. BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked).

CONFLICTS BETWEEN UK SOURCES (kept as separate items/rules):
- Statins and breastfeeding: Lipitor and Zocor SmPCs say contraindicated / must not breastfeed; SPS says atorvastatin (preferred) and simvastatin (others preferred) can be used with caution with infant monitoring.
- Clopidogrel and breastfeeding: Plavix SmPC says breastfeeding should not be continued; SPS says use with caution with infant monitoring.
- Clopidogrel and pregnancy: Plavix SmPC says preferable not to use; BUMPS says it can be used if prescribed by a doctor when benefits outweigh risks.
- Warfarin SmPCs: Marevan (emc 2803) lists oral anti-diabetic agents and diuretics (also anabolic steroids, cimetidine, clofibrate, chloramphenicol, moxifloxacin, miconazole) as potentiating warfarin; the Strides generic (emc 14333) does not list oral anti-diabetics or diuretics. Strides adds 'preferably on an empty stomach' and baseline PT/INR before starting. Rules for group:oral-antidiabetic and group:diuretic cite Marevan only.
- Atorvastatin + clarithromycin: current Lipitor SmPC says avoid if possible, otherwise consider lower starting and maximum doses with monitoring (its Table 1 is merged-cell and the exact cap for clarithromycin is ambiguous in flat text). SPS (2024) and MHRA DSU (2008 article) both state maximum atorvastatin 20 mg daily if unavoidable. The MHRA 2008 article is old; its simvastatin advice is superseded by the 2012 DSUs (e.g. amlodipine cap now 20 mg/day).
- Renal: simvastatin SmPC uses creatinine clearance < 30 ml/min (doses above 10 mg/day carefully considered); SPS statins monitoring uses eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m2 (check dose with renal specialist). Both kept.

INTERACTIONS NOT FOUND in the accessed batch-C sources (not added): warfarin with clarithromycin, ciprofloxacin, trimethoprim, amoxicillin, levothyroxine, metformin by name (only 'oral anti-diabetic agents' in Marevan) - these may be stated in the other medicine's own SmPC (batches D/E/F). Warfarin SmPCs name erythromycin (not clarithromycin) and moxifloxacin (not ciprofloxacin). Clopidogrel + ciprofloxacin comes only from the MHRA 2010 DSU list of CYP2C19 inhibitors, not the current Plavix SmPC. Atorvastatin + amlodipine and + magnesium/aluminium antacid: SmPC gives 'No specific recommendation' (item only, no rule).

GROUP RULES THAT DEPEND ON MEMBERSHIP FROM OTHER BATCHES: warfarin uses group:oral-antidiabetic (member: metformin), group:diuretic (member: spironolactone), group:corticosteroid (no members yet); clopidogrel uses group:opioid. This batch did not define members for these groups. This batch defines nsaid (ibuprofen, naproxen), ssri (sertraline), ppi and cyp2c19-inhibitor (omeprazole; ciprofloxacin via MHRA), strong-cyp3a4-inhibitor (clarithromycin), statin, antiplatelet, anticoagulant, vitamin-k-antagonist.

Warfarin + co-trimoxazole rule is based on the SmPC naming sulfamethoxazole (an ingredient of co-trimoxazole).
Warfarin + tramadol: MHRA DSU June 2024 (not yet in the warfarin SmPC text).
Brand-specific prescribing: none stated by any accessed UK source for these medicines.
Formulations not covered: warfarin oral suspension (emc 5766), simvastatin oral suspension, clopidogrel 300 mg tablets (loading), Neokay and generic phytomenadione products. Konakion MM 10 mg/ml is IV only (IM contraindicated); oral use of the IV preparation appears in the warfarin SmPC overdose section and SPS calls it off-label.
Zocor SmPC covers 10/20/40 mg; the 80 mg strength is from the Brown & Burk generic SmPC (emc 10668), checked for matching contraindications and renal advice.

AUDIT 2026-10-17 (second checker, see audit/C.md): warfarin:interaction:antibacterial (group:antibacterial) removed because the group also holds dapsone, trimethoprim and others that the SmPC sentence ('broad spectrum antibiotics') does not name; named antibiotic interactions are carried by the antibiotics' own rules (amoxicillin, co-amoxiclav, clarithromycin, ciprofloxacin, co-trimoxazole, trimethoprim) plus warfarin:interaction:trimethoprim and warfarin:interaction:co-trimoxazole here. Warfarin 'planned surgery' rule lowered to caution; the 4.3 contraindication is now its own condition (post-major-surgery-72h). Pregnancy rules for statins and clopidogrel split by source (SmPC vs BUMPS). New conditions: phenylketonuria (Lipitor chewable aspartame), post-major-surgery-72h. mhra-tmp-tab-teva (also in batch F, same URL) added here because warfarin:interaction:trimethoprim cites it. BACK-FILL 2026-10-17 (new master-list medicines): rules added from the SmPCs already used. Warfarin (Marevan emc 2803 / Strides emc 14333 + SPS warfarin monitoring): SNRIs (group:snri) and aspirin avoid; miconazole caution; azole antifungals (group), allopurinol, fibrates (group), metronidazole, moxifloxacin (Marevan only) and carbamazepine (antagonist) monitor. Not added: 'broad spectrum antibiotics' (no named drug), erythromycin (not in list), 'oestrogens'/'oral contraceptives' (no master-list oral contraceptive; estriol-lactobacillus is vaginal), desvenlafaxine (no UK product file, not in group:snri). Existing warfarin:interaction:corticosteroid uses group:corticosteroid, which now also holds nasal/inhaled steroids; the engine does not apply group rules to nasal products, but budesonide nebuliser (inhalation) will match. Atorvastatin (Lipitor): diltiazem, verapamil, fluconazole (moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors) and group:fibrate at dose level ('lower maximum/starting dose should be considered' + monitoring); ezetimibe caution; carbamazepine info (CYP3A inducer). Systemic fusidic acid rule not added: the master-list fusidic acid products are topical only. Simvastatin: verapamil and diltiazem dose (max 20 mg daily); fluconazole caution (Zocor) AND a separate contraindicated rule from the Brown & Burk 80 mg SmPC (emc 10668), which lists fluconazole among potent CYP3A4 inhibitors whose combination is contraindicated while also listing it under caution - CONFLICT, both kept; fenofibrate caution. Clopidogrel (Plavix): aspirin caution; fluoxetine, fluconazole, carbamazepine avoid (named as strong/moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors, 'should be discouraged'); repaglinide caution (CYP2C8); rosuvastatin info. Pantoprazole: Plavix says clopidogrel 'can be administered with pantoprazole' - no rule. Phytomenadione: nothing new (4.5 names coumarins only).
